domain_label: Study System — Engagement, Gamification & Progress Visuals (engage): the ephemeral, quarantined session-drill WaterMeter timed-fluency mechanic and its four-gate guardrails
purpose: A method for deciding whether a timed-drill / decaying-resource-meter / variable-reward / collection engagement mechanic may ship in a single-user study app — the opt-in, isolated automaticity drill over small MCQs on the existing-but-unused skill_drill surface, with an ephemeral non-persisted WaterMeter, session-only decay framed as momentum not forgetting, a deterministic correct-within-window rise, a game_timed evidence quarantine and one-way read-only arrow, timeout != wrong, honest collection mapped to real mastered units, and a blue-not-green stepped tickless encoding — judging each against engage's four gates (fidelity, motivation-safety, guardrails, learning-primacy) and the ten GAMIFICATION_PLAN invariants, so the drill is a conditional GO only when every gate holds and a no-go otherwise, with every external claim tagged FACT / ESTIMATE / UNKNOWN exactly as the grounding plan did and no statistic invented that the recon did not verify.
assumptions: the single learner is the only user and there is no leaderboard, social comparison or tangible-reward economy in scope; the drill meter is judged as informational fluency feedback to one person, never as a currency or a points-for-prizes system

the drill is opt-in, isolated from the FSRS-scheduled Review, and built on the existing-but-unused Card.kind=skill_drill surface [FACT - APP_RECON 6.11]; its reward meter is ephemeral, quarantined from the learning model, and visually unmistakable from real progress [ESTIMATE - plan section 1/2]

the design is a heuristic prior from the GAMIFICATION_PLAN, not an observed dataset; this KB introduces no measured drill outcome, so observed_impact and data_quality stay 0.0 exactly as the sibling gamification KB's evidence_label_policy mandates

the only FACT-grade app-behaviour claims available are the plan's recon tags [FACT - APP_RECON 6.11] (skill_drill surface exists, unused) and [FACT - APP_RECON 5] (no animation/physics lib today); every other drill-design claim is [ESTIMATE - design] or an [UNKNOWN] open decision

several load-bearing constants are owner-open build-time decisions the plan did not fix (water_decay_timescale, game_answer_logging, the TOEFL wrong-answer penalty, and the graphux build-vs-adopt animation choice) and are carried as [UNKNOWN], never invented
exclusions: the FSRS scheduling algorithm, interval math and backlog ordering belong to the scheduler/SRS specialist; this KB only constrains that the drill never writes to or degrades that output (the quarantine and session-only-decay rules)

the learner-model internals (BKT mastery estimation, ItemElo, CalibrationBin) belong to the learner-model specialist and are referenced only as the read-only source of the real mastery threshold the honest collection consumes, never written by the drill

the motion and physics implementation (the drop animation, the build-vs-adopt of an animation lib) belongs to the graphux specialist; engage constrains it (removable physics, reduced-motion fallback, static targets) but does not build it

exact visual styling beyond the owner-fixed separation semantics (the precise cyan hex, pixel sizes, easing curves, the exact fall-time constant and decay_per_sec value) is a build-time decision routed to graphux/uxguide
inventing a drill engagement lift, fluency-gain, retention or completion statistic the recon did not verify, or presenting a design estimate as an observed finding

competency_questions.question: What exactly is the fenced brief for the session drill, and which parts are binding versus held open?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRILL_SCOPE_FIDELITY records the opt-in timed fluency drill on the unused Card.kind=skill_drill surface [FACT - APP_RECON 6.11] with the ephemeral/quarantined/visually-unmistakable binding properties, and lists water_decay_timescale, game_answer_logging and the TOEFL penalty as [UNKNOWN] held-open decisions, never invented

competency_questions.question: What is the ephemeral WaterMeter data model, and how is non-persistence guaranteed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WATERMETER_MODEL gives WaterMeter { level 0..100 stepped, rise_per_hit, decay_per_sec, window_ms } as a non-persisted client/session object that resets each session and writes nothing to day-box pct, course mastery, LearnerState/BKT, ItemElo, FSRS CardState or CalibrationBin

competency_questions.question: What does the rise rule honestly reward, and why is that a tension against the retention invariant?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WATER_RISE_RULE states rise fires only on correct-within-window as speed+accuracy=recognition fluency with a deterministic rise_per_hit, flags it 'speed not mastery', and marks it a conditional PASS that collides with INV-5 and clears only because DRILL_CONTENT_ELIGIBILITY fences it to automaticity-only content

competency_questions.question: Why must the decay be session-only, and why is multi-day decay rejected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SESSION_DECAY_RULE frames decay as session momentum not forgetting, requires it be session-only, and rejects multi-day decay because it creates a pull to review early (a spacing violation failing INV-2 and INV-4), keeping water_decay_timescale [UNKNOWN] with session-only recommended

competency_questions.question: How is the timed drill kept construct-valid for the underlying MCQ and for ESL fairness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIMED_DRILL_MODE keeps the MCQ unchanged and still gated (cover-the-options, homogeneous options, real-error distractors), sets a per-card fall window with a readable ESL floor, and makes the static option buttons the selection target so no moving drop turns it into a motor-dexterity test

competency_questions.question: How is timed-mode evidence quarantined from the learning model, and why is flag-and-trust insufficient?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUARANTINE_INVARIANT logs timed data only as evidence_class=game_timed excluded by default from every BKT/Elo replay, diagnosis and calibration bin, keeps the arrow one-way (read never write), and re-verifies every bkt_evidence/submitReview change because that path was silently broken once already (INV-10)

competency_questions.question: Why is a missed drop not a wrong answer, and what does it write to the learner model?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TIMEOUT_NOT_WRONG states a missed drop has no chosen_option_id, is not an FSRS Again, carries no misconception, writes no learning-model evidence, and surfaces 'Correct - but the drop fell first. Speed, not knowledge' with an untimed re-see, encoding INV-8

competency_questions.question: Which content is eligible for the timed drill and which is prohibited, and why?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRILL_CONTENT_ELIGIBILITY routes remember/understand terminology gates and time-boxed TOEFL small tasks in, and routes INBDE itemsets/vignettes/EXCEPT-NOT/constructed-response out because timing them trains recognition-over-understanding, with the TOEFL wrong-answer penalty held [UNKNOWN]

competency_questions.question: When is a collection mechanic honest, and when does it become a no-go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_COLLECTION lights KG concepts only at a real BKT mastery threshold (never on drill hits and never reading the WaterMeter), which is the 'all zeros' fix and maps to a real denominator (G3), and becomes a NO-GO the moment a 'concept unlocked by drill speed' variant is proposed

competency_questions.question: Why are variable/random reward schedules rejected, and what does that require of rise_per_hit?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VARIABLE_REWARD_REJECT rejects variable/random reward schedules as a dark pattern that breaks the informational-feedback rule (overjustification) and therefore requires rise_per_hit to be deterministic so the WaterMeter never becomes a variable-ratio slot-machine

competency_questions.question: How is the drill meter made visually unmistakable from real mastery progress?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HONEST_DRILL_ENCODING separates the meter by form (a vertical tank), hue (blue, outside the mastery green/yellow/red palette), location (drill surface only) and label+no-persistence, quantises the fill into discrete steps, and keeps it tickless (the completion tick is reserved for real day-box completion)

competency_questions.question: What accessibility floor does the drill require, and what stays independent of the decorative motion?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRILL_ACCESSIBILITY requires prefers-reduced-motion to fall back to a static countdown numeral/ring + step meter (drop physics removable, timer information not), colorblind reads by height + numeric label, no shame loop, onboarding pre-explains timeout, and flags graphux build-vs-adopt [UNKNOWN] since no animation lib exists today [FACT - APP_RECON 5]

competency_questions.question: When is the session drill a go, and what makes it a no-go?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRILL_GO_NOGO composes the verdict: the drill is a CONDITIONAL GO only when it clears G1 fidelity, G2 motivation-safety (deterministic rise, no variable reward), G3 guardrails (quarantine, timeout != wrong, ESL floor, static target, honest collection) and G4 learning-primacy (non-persistence, one-way arrow, session-only decay) at once; failing any gate is a no-go until fixed, and it ships LAST behind graphux

glossary.definition: The drill's session-flow meter WaterMeter { level 0..100 rendered stepped, rise_per_hit, decay_per_sec, window_ms }: a non-persisted client/session object that resets each session and writes nothing to the learning model. A coarse fluency counter, never a measured mastery continuum [ESTIMATE - design, plan section 1].

The rule that timed-mode answers are logged only as a distinct evidence_class=game_timed (extending grade_source) and excluded by default from every nightly BKT/Elo replay, diagnosis and calibration bin; the arrow is one-way (the game reads the model, never writes it) [ESTIMATE - design, plan section 3 INV-3/INV-9].

level -= decay_per_sec * dt floored at 0, framed as session momentum ('use it or lose it this session'), NOT forgetting. It must never persist across days; multi-day decay is rejected because it creates a spacing-violating pull to review early [ESTIMATE - design, plan section 1; water_decay_timescale UNKNOWN].

A missed drop has no chosen_option_id, so it is not a misconception, not a knowledge verdict, and never an FSRS 'Again'; it writes no learning-model evidence and offers an untimed re-see. A game clock never substitutes for the learner-model latency/honesty signal (INV-8) [ESTIMATE - design, plan section 1].

What the rise rule honestly rewards: correctness-within-a-window = speed + accuracy = recognition fluency, valid only where automaticity is the objective and always UI-flagged as speed not mastery; unflagged, it is a no-go [ESTIMATE - design, plan section 1].

A collection mechanic that lights up KG concepts only when they reach a real BKT mastery threshold, never from accrued drill hits and never by reading the WaterMeter; the concrete fix for 'all zeros' and an anti-illusionary mapping to a real denominator [ESTIMATE - design, plan section 2.3].

The standing rejection of variable/random (variable-ratio) reward schedules as a dark pattern adjacent to a tangible-reward economy that breaks the informational-feedback rule; it requires rise_per_hit to be deterministic so the meter never becomes a slot-machine [ESTIMATE - design synthesis, plan section 2].

The four honest-encoding separators of the drill meter from real mastery: form (a vertical tank), hue (blue, outside the green/yellow/red mastery palette), location (drill surface only) and label+no-persistence; the fill is quantised into discrete steps and is tickless (the completion tick is reserved for real day-box completion) [ESTIMATE - design, plan section 1].

The readable minimum on the per-card fall window, calibrated to option count and ESL reading rate, so the timer measures recognition fluency and not English reading speed; never a fixed cinematic constant [ESTIMATE - design, plan section 1].

engage's ship gates the drill must clear at once: G1 fidelity (faithful and visually unmistakable), G2 motivation-safety (informational, deterministic, no variable reward), G3 guardrails (quarantine, timeout != wrong, ESL floor, static target, honest collection), G4 learning-primacy (non-persistence, one-way arrow, session-only decay). Fail any gate = no-go [ESTIMATE - design synthesis].

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for the session-drill mechanics work units in absence of supplied datasets; the design is grounded in the GAMIFICATION_PLAN and its APP_RECON tags, carried at the plan's own FACT/ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN grade
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; GAMIFICATION_PLAN design synthesis; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Anchor the drill to the owner request as recorded in the plan: an opt-in timed warm-up / fluency drill over a pool of small MCQs, separate from the FSRS-scheduled Review, on the existing-but-unused Card.kind="skill_drill" surface [FACT — APP_RECON §6.11]. Binding properties every other node inherits: the reward meter is ephemeral, quarantined from the learning model, and visually unmistakable from real progress [ESTIMATE — plan §1/§2]. This node does not itself ship a mechanic; it fixes the fence and is the G1-fidelity reference, carrying the framing 'gamify the wall, not the hole.' Held-open decisions are kept, not invented: water_decay_timescale, game_answer_logging, and the TOEFL wrong-answer penalty are all [UNKNOWN — plan §5]. The whole drill is a conditional GO, narrowly fenced, and ships LAST behind the new graphux specialist.

included: the opt-in / timed / fluency / skill_drill-surface fenced brief as recorded in the plan
the ephemeral + quarantined + visually-unmistakable binding properties every node inherits
the held-open decisions (water_decay_timescale, game_answer_logging, TOEFL penalty) tagged UNKNOWN
excluded: the meter data model itself (its own node)
the four-gate verdict (the synthesis node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an owner clarification on a held-open decision (water_decay_timescale, game_answer_logging, TOEFL penalty) or a plan revision changes the fence

pros.claim: Fixing the fence first stops a later engineer widening the drill past the opt-in, isolated, ephemeral scope the owner set
pros.example: building the drill on the existing Card.kind=skill_drill surface rather than bolting timers onto the FSRS Review

cons.claim: Several load-bearing constants are genuinely unresolved, so the fence is exact in shape but open in a few numbers
cons.example: the decay timescale being stated as session-only in intent while the actual constant stays [UNKNOWN] until the owner fixes it

failure_modes: widening the drill beyond the opt-in isolated automaticity scope
inventing a value for a held-open decision instead of flagging it UNKNOWN
acceptance_tests: the brief states the drill is opt-in, timed, fluency-only, on the skill_drill surface, and separate from FSRS Review, with the ephemeral/quarantined/visually-unmistakable properties as [ESTIMATE] and the three held-open constants as [UNKNOWN]
revisit_triggers: the owner resolves a held-open constant
a downstream node contradicts a binding property

nodes.definition: Define the ephemeral session-flow meter data model [ESTIMATE — design from plan §1]: WaterMeter { level: 0..100 rendered STEPPED not smooth, rise_per_hit, decay_per_sec, window_ms } as a client/session state object, non-persisted. Non-persistence invariant: it resets each session and writes NOTHING to day-box pct, course mastery, LearnerState/BKT, ItemElo, FSRS CardState, or CalibrationBin. G4 PASS via non-persistence (INV-1 no BKT/Elo write, INV-2 no interval write, INV-9 one-way arrow); the meter is a fluency counter, not a currency (G2); the STEPPED render is the G1 hook — a coarse counter, never a measured continuum.

included: the WaterMeter { level 0..100 stepped, rise_per_hit, decay_per_sec, window_ms } fields
the non-persistence invariant (writes nothing to BKT/Elo/FSRS/CalibrationBin/day-box/course)
the stepped-not-smooth render as the coarse-counter G1 hook
excluded: the rise and decay mutation rules (their own nodes)
the game_timed logging path (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a persistence or schema change touches the meter, or a new drill surface reads/writes the level

pros.claim: A non-persisted session object makes the learning-model firewall structural, not a matter of discipline
pros.example: the meter living only in client/session state so a page reload zeroes it and no nightly job can read it

cons.claim: A purely session object cannot show cross-session fluency trend, which some designs would want
cons.example: a learner who wants a week-over-week fluency chart cannot get one from an object that resets each session

failure_modes: persisting the level into any durable store
letting the render imply a smooth measured continuum rather than a coarse stepped counter
acceptance_tests: the model defines the four WaterMeter fields, marks the object non-persisted/session-scoped, and asserts it writes nothing to day-box pct, course mastery, BKT, Elo, FSRS CardState or CalibrationBin
revisit_triggers: a persistence or caching change touches the meter
a new surface wants to read the level

nodes.definition: Rise fires ONLY when correct == true AND within the fall window: level = min(100, level + rise_per_hit); otherwise the drop disappears [ESTIMATE — plan §1]. What it honestly rewards is correctness-within-a-window = speed + accuracy = recognition fluency, valid ONLY where automaticity is the actual objective, flagged as such in the UI and never sold as mastery. rise_per_hit is deterministic/fixed, guarding against variable-reward drift. This is the tension node: rewarding speed collides with INV-5 (never reward raw speed/volume over retention); it clears the gate ONLY because it is fenced to automaticity-only content (DRILL_CONTENT_ELIGIBILITY) and quarantined (QUARANTINE_INVARIANT). G2 is a conditional-PASS contingent on the honesty label; without the 'speed, not mastery' flag it is a NO-GO.

included: the correct-within-window rise rule and deterministic rise_per_hit
the honest 'speed + accuracy = recognition fluency' claim and its mandatory UI flag
the INV-5 tension and the fence/quarantine conditions that clear it
excluded: the timed-mode fall window mechanics (its own node)
the content routing that legitimises the reward (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the honesty label is dropped, rise_per_hit is made variable, or the fenced content set changes

pros.claim: Naming exactly what the rise rewards (fluency, not mastery) keeps the mechanic honest and auditable
pros.example: the UI labelling a filled meter 'recognition speed' so it is never mistaken for course mastery

cons.claim: Rewarding speed is intrinsically in tension with the retention invariant and only survives inside a tight fence
cons.example: the same rule applied to an apply/analyze item would reward fast guessing over understanding

failure_modes: dropping the 'speed, not mastery' label so the reward masquerades as competence
making rise_per_hit variable and drifting toward a variable-ratio reward
acceptance_tests: rise fires only on correct-within-window, rise_per_hit is deterministic, the UI flags it as speed/fluency not mastery, and the node states it clears G2 only under the content fence and the quarantine

nodes.definition: level -= decay_per_sec · dt, floored at 0, framed as session momentum ('use it or lose it THIS session'), NOT forgetting/retrievability — calling it 'forgetting' would falsely borrow the FSRS concept [ESTIMATE — plan §1]. DECAY MUST BE SESSION-ONLY, never over days. Multi-day decay is REJECTED because it creates a pull to review early = a spacing violation (fails INV-2 and INV-4, punishing a spacing-correct rest day). The open decision water_decay_timescale is [UNKNOWN — owner states the constant, plan §5], with session-only recommended and multi-day rejected. The node's job is to encode the rejection so a later engineer cannot 'improve retention' by persisting decay across days.

included: the session-momentum decay rule floored at 0 and its non-forgetting framing
the session-only requirement and the explicit multi-day rejection
the water_decay_timescale UNKNOWN and its recommended session-only resolution
excluded: the meter fields (its own node)
the go/no-go composition (the synthesis node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the owner fixes water_decay_timescale, or any proposal tries to persist decay across days

pros.claim: Encoding multi-day decay as REJECTED prevents a well-meaning 'retention' change from creating a spacing-violating pull to review early
pros.example: refusing to persist the meter overnight so the app never nudges a learner to drill on a scheduled rest day

cons.claim: The exact decay constant is unset, so session pacing feel is tunable but not yet fixed
cons.example: two different decay_per_sec values giving very different session urgency, unresolved until the owner picks one

failure_modes: persisting decay across days and creating a review-early pull
framing the decay as 'forgetting' and borrowing the FSRS retrievability concept
acceptance_tests: the rule is session-scoped and floored at 0, framed as momentum not forgetting, multi-day decay is explicitly rejected as an INV-2/INV-4 violation, and water_decay_timescale is carried [UNKNOWN] with session-only recommended
revisit_triggers: the owner fixes the decay constant

nodes.definition: The timed drill mode itself. The fall window is a per-card ESTIMATE calibrated to option count + ESL reading rate, with a readable floor, never a fixed cinematic constant [ESTIMATE — plan §1]. The MCQ under the animation is unchanged: it must still pass the full ship gate (cover-the-options, homogeneous options, real-error distractors, no testwiseness cues) — 'a gamified item that fails cover-the-options is a broken item wearing an animation.' Selection targets are the STATIC option buttons (keys 1—4 / tap), never a moving drop (clicking a moving target is a motor-dexterity test, construct-invalid). G1 fidelity + construct-validity; the fall-time floor is the ESL-fairness guard so the timer does not silently test English reading rate.

included: the per-card fall window with a readable ESL floor
the unchanged-MCQ ship-gate requirement under the animation
the static-option-button selection rule (never a moving drop)
excluded: the timeout semantics (its own node)
the accessibility constraints (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the fall-window calibration or the selection-target rule changes, or a new item type enters the mode

pros.claim: Keeping the selection target the static option buttons preserves the measured construct instead of testing motor dexterity
pros.example: pressing key 2 to answer while the drop is purely decorative timing, not a target to be clicked

cons.claim: A per-card fall window is harder to calibrate than a fixed constant and can still mis-time an item
cons.example: an unusually long stem timing out fast learners if the reading-rate floor is set too low

failure_modes: making a moving drop the click target and turning the item into a dexterity test
using a fixed cinematic fall constant that silently tests English reading rate
acceptance_tests: the fall window is per-card with an ESL-reading-rate floor, the underlying MCQ still passes the full item ship gate, and selection is on the static option buttons never a moving target
revisit_triggers: a new item type is admitted

nodes.definition: The load-bearing node. Timed-mode data is quarantined: logged only as a distinct evidence_class = "game_timed" (extend grade_source) and excluded BY DEFAULT from every nightly BKT/Elo replay, diagnosis, and calibration bin [ESTIMATE — plan §3 INV-3]. Flag-and-trust is insufficient — the bkt_evidence path was silently broken once already — so every change touching bkt_evidence/submitReview is re-verified, never reverted-and-trusted (INV-10). The arrow is one-way: the game READS the model, never writes it (INV-9). This encodes INV-1, INV-2, INV-3, INV-9 and INV-10 and is the cornerstone of G4. Open decision game_answer_logging: quarantine-and-exclude (recommended) vs a retained game_timed side-metric that needs the schema change + re-verification BEFORE any writer ships [UNKNOWN — plan §5].

included: the game_timed evidence_class and its default exclusion from replay/diagnosis/calibration
the re-verify-never-revert-and-trust rule on bkt_evidence/submitReview
the one-way read-only arrow and the game_answer_logging UNKNOWN
excluded: the meter model it protects (its own node)
the four gates it feeds (the synthesis node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any change touches bkt_evidence/submitReview/grade_source, or game_answer_logging is resolved toward a retained side-metric

pros.claim: A distinct evidence_class excluded by default makes contamination the exception a writer must justify, not the default
pros.example: a nightly BKT replay skipping every game_timed row so a fast drill never shifts a mastery estimate

cons.claim: A retained game_timed side-metric would need the schema change and re-verification before any writer ships, so the safe default is exclusion
cons.example: adding a game_timed analytics table and only later discovering a join silently fed it into calibration

failure_modes: letting game_timed rows into any BKT/Elo replay, diagnosis, or calibration bin
trusting a flag change on the bkt_evidence path without re-verifying it
acceptance_tests: timed answers are logged only as evidence_class=game_timed excluded by default from replay/diagnosis/calibration, the arrow is one-way read-only, and any bkt_evidence/submitReview change is re-verified rather than reverted-and-trusted
revisit_triggers: a change touches the bkt_evidence or submitReview path
a new consumer of grade_source appears

nodes.definition: A missed drop has NO chosen_option_id, so it carries no misconception, no knowledge verdict, and is NOT an FSRS 'Again' [ESTIMATE — plan §1]. UI: 'Correct — but the drop fell first. Speed, not knowledge,' with an offer to re-see the item untimed; it writes no learning-model evidence. This is the biggest validity trap: it encodes INV-8 (a game clock never stands in for the learner model's latency/honesty signal) and G4, with no shame loop.

included: a missed drop carries no chosen_option_id, no verdict, and is not an FSRS Again
the 'speed, not knowledge' UI copy and the untimed re-see offer
INV-8: a game clock never substitutes for the learner-model latency/honesty signal
excluded: the fall-window mode that produces the timeout (its own node)
the game_timed logging path (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a proposal maps a timeout onto an FSRS grade or a learner-model latency signal

pros.claim: Refusing to map a timeout onto 'Again' keeps a running-out-of-time event from corrupting the schedule as a fake lapse
pros.example: a learner who knew the answer but was slow keeps their real FSRS interval intact

cons.claim: Offering an untimed re-see adds a UI branch and a second interaction the drill must handle
cons.example: a learner repeatedly timing out and re-seeing untimed, lengthening the session

failure_modes: logging a timeout as an FSRS Again or any error signal
showing a shame/failure loop on a missed drop
acceptance_tests: a missed drop writes no learning-model evidence, is never an FSRS Again, surfaces 'speed, not knowledge' copy with an untimed re-see, and encodes INV-8
revisit_triggers: a timeout is proposed as a grade
a latency signal wants to read the clock

nodes.definition: Hard content routing [ESTIMATE — plan §1, qcraft]. ELIGIBLE: INBDE standalone remember/understand terminology gates (anatomy/structure naming, drug-class recognition, definition recall — short homogeneous options); TOEFL already-time-boxed small tasks (Complete-the-Words, possibly Listen-and-Choose), gated current-2026-vs-legacy. PROHIBITED: INBDE itemsets/cases, any vignette apply/analyze item, EXCEPT/NOT items, and all constructed-response/productive tasks — timing these trains recognition-over-understanding, the exact INBDE anti-goal. INBDE no-penalty timeout is grounded; the TOEFL wrong-answer penalty is [UNKNOWN] (no-penalty only by analogy, plan §5). This node is what makes the speed-reward legitimate: it fences the fluency reward to the only place automaticity is the real objective (G1 + construct-validity).

included: the ELIGIBLE remember/understand terminology and time-boxed TOEFL small-task list
the PROHIBITED itemsets/vignettes/EXCEPT-NOT/constructed-response list
the INBDE no-penalty grounding and the TOEFL-penalty UNKNOWN
excluded: the timed-mode mechanics (its own node)
the speed-reward rule it legitimises (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the eligible/prohibited routing changes, or the TOEFL wrong-answer penalty is resolved

pros.claim: Fencing the drill to automaticity-only content is exactly what makes rewarding speed defensible
pros.example: timing drug-class recognition, where fast recall is the real objective, while never timing a case vignette

cons.claim: The TOEFL wrong-answer penalty is only analogised from INBDE, so one eligible surface has an open scoring question
cons.example: assuming no-penalty for a timed TOEFL task when its real scoring rule is still [UNKNOWN]

failure_modes: admitting an apply/analyze vignette or itemset into the timed drill
timing a constructed-response or EXCEPT/NOT item and training recognition-over-understanding
acceptance_tests: the node lists eligible remember/understand terminology and time-boxed TOEFL tasks, prohibits itemsets/vignettes/EXCEPT-NOT/constructed-response, and carries the TOEFL penalty [UNKNOWN]
revisit_triggers: a new item type is proposed for the drill

nodes.definition: A collection mechanic is honest only when it maps to real mastered units: KG concepts light up as they reach a REAL BKT mastery threshold, not when the learner accrues drill hits [ESTIMATE — plan §2.3]. This is the concrete fix for 'all zeros' and is honest collection (real mastered units, not vanity badges, not fluency-meter hits). G3 PASS (progress maps to a real denominator — anti-illusionary) and G4 via the one-way arrow (it READS BKT mastery, never writes). It becomes a NO-GO the moment a 'concept unlocked by drill speed' variant is proposed — that would be illusionary progress. The collection must NOT read the WaterMeter.

included: the real-BKT-mastery-threshold unlock rule for KG concepts
the 'all zeros' fix and the not-vanity / not-fluency-hits honesty line
the must-not-read-the-WaterMeter constraint
excluded: the meter's rise rule it must not read (its own node)
the mastery-model internals (routed to the learner-model specialist)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a 'concept unlocked by drill speed' variant is proposed, or the mastery threshold source changes

pros.claim: Tying the collection to a real BKT mastery threshold makes a lit-up concept a truthful claim of learning
pros.example: a KG node turning gold only once its BKT mastery crosses threshold, so the map reflects real competence

cons.claim: A mastery-gated collection lights up more slowly than a hit-gated one, which can feel less immediately rewarding
cons.example: early sessions showing few lit concepts because real mastery, unlike drill hits, accrues slowly

failure_modes: unlocking a collected concept from drill speed or accrued fluency hits
letting the collection read the WaterMeter instead of the mastery model
acceptance_tests: concepts light up only at a real BKT mastery threshold, never from drill hits or the WaterMeter, and the node names the 'unlocked by drill speed' variant an illusionary-progress NO-GO
revisit_triggers: a drill-speed unlock variant is proposed

nodes.definition: Variable/random reward schedules are REJECTED (plan §2 REJECT list; engage anti-patterns; learner/scheduler concurrence) [ESTIMATE — design synthesis]. Consequence for this KB: rise_per_hit must be deterministic — the WaterMeter must never become a variable-ratio slot-machine. A variable-ratio schedule is a dark pattern adjacent to a tangible-reward economy and breaks the informational-feedback rule (overjustification), so any variable-reward variant is a G2 motivation-safety FAIL / NO-GO. This node is named explicitly as a standing rejection so the drill cannot drift into a compulsion loop, mirroring how the existing KB carries ILLUSIONARY_PROGRESS_ETHICS.

included: the standing rejection of variable/random reward schedules
the deterministic-rise_per_hit consequence for the WaterMeter
the overjustification / dark-pattern rationale
excluded: the rise rule it constrains (its own node)
the go/no-go composition (the synthesis node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any variable/random reward schedule is proposed for the meter or the collection

pros.claim: A standing named rejection stops a future 'make it more fun' change from installing a variable-ratio compulsion loop
pros.example: refusing to randomise rise_per_hit into a jackpot so the meter never becomes a slot-machine

cons.claim: A strictly deterministic reward is less novelty-rich than a variable one, trading engagement lift for safety
cons.example: a fixed rise feeling predictable compared with a variable schedule that would be more habit-forming but manipulative

failure_modes: randomising rise_per_hit into a variable-ratio schedule
adding any jackpot/loot reward adjacent to a tangible-reward economy
acceptance_tests: the node rejects variable/random reward schedules, requires deterministic rise_per_hit, and marks any variable-reward variant a G2 no-go on overjustification/dark-pattern grounds

nodes.definition: The four honest-encoding separators from real mastery [ESTIMATE — plan §1, viz]: form (a vertical tank, not a mastery bar/line); hue (a cool/cyan token OUTSIDE the mastery green/yellow/red palette — blue, not green); location (drill surface only — never the Dashboard or Learner-Model page); and label + no persistence ('session,' writes nowhere). Fill is quantized into discrete steps (like the DayBox floor(...*20)) signalling 'coarse counter,' and it is tickless — the completion tick is reserved for real day-box completion and must never appear on the meter. G1 fidelity — 'visually unmistakable from real progress' — directly reusing and protecting the existing KBs' terminal-tick invariant and the green-mastery palette.

included: the four separators: form (tank), hue (blue-not-green), location (drill-only), label+no-persistence
the discrete-step quantisation signalling a coarse counter
the tickless rule reserving the completion tick for real day-box completion
excluded: the meter fields (its own node)
reduced-motion / colorblind a11y (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the meter is placed on a mastery surface, colored green, or given a completion tick

pros.claim: Four independent separators make the meter visually unmistakable from real mastery even if one is missed
pros.example: a blue vertical tank on the drill screen that no learner would confuse with the green day-box fill

cons.claim: A deliberately-different visual language for the meter adds a second design vocabulary to maintain
cons.example: designers having to keep the blue drill palette and the green mastery palette consistently distinct

failure_modes: coloring the meter in the mastery green/yellow/red palette
placing the meter on the Dashboard or Learner-Model page, or giving it a completion tick
acceptance_tests: the meter is a blue vertical tank on the drill surface only, stepped/quantized, session-labeled, non-persisted, and tickless (the completion tick stays reserved for real day-box completion)
revisit_triggers: the meter is proposed for a mastery surface
the day-box tick invariant is revisited

nodes.definition: Hard requirements [ESTIMATE — plan §1, uxguide]: prefers-reduced-motion → a static countdown numeral/ring + discrete step meter (drop physics is decorative and FULLY removable; the timer INFORMATION is not). Colorblind → level reads by height + numeric label, never green/red water alone. No shame loop on wrong/timeout; first-run onboarding pre-explains the timeout framing. graphux owns the motion; engage constrains it — the app has no animation/physics lib today [FACT — APP_RECON §5], and build-vs-adopt is [UNKNOWN] until prototyped. The removability rule keeps the timer information (the real signal) independent of the decorative juice (construct-validity + honesty gate).

included: the reduced-motion static-countdown + step-meter requirement (physics removable, timer info not)
the colorblind height + numeric-label requirement
the no-shame-loop, onboarding pre-explanation, and graphux build-vs-adopt UNKNOWN
excluded: the motion implementation (owned by graphux)
the timed-mode selection rules (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: graphux resolves build-vs-adopt for the motion, or a reduced-motion/colorblind gap is found

pros.claim: Making the drop physics fully removable while the timer information stays keeps the real signal independent of the juice
pros.example: a reduced-motion user seeing a static countdown ring and step meter with the same timing information, no animation

cons.claim: The animation approach is unresolved (no lib today, build-vs-adopt open), so the motion layer is not yet costed
cons.example: not knowing whether a physics lib is adopted or built until graphux prototypes it

failure_modes: removing the timer information along with the decorative physics under reduced-motion
encoding level by green/red water alone with no height or numeric label
acceptance_tests: reduced-motion falls back to a static countdown + step meter with the timer information preserved, level reads by height + numeric label, there is no shame loop, and build-vs-adopt is flagged [UNKNOWN]
revisit_triggers: a reduced-motion or colorblind gap is reported

nodes.definition: The synthesis node (analogue of ENGAGEMENT_GO_NOGO). The drill is a CONDITIONAL GO only when it clears all four gates at once [ESTIMATE — design synthesis]: G1 Fidelity — faithful to the plan spec AND visually unmistakable from real progress (blue/tank/tickless/session-labeled, stepped) [N1, N11]; G2 Motivation-safety — informational fluency feedback with the 'speed, not mastery' label, deterministic rise, NO variable reward, no points/currency [N3, N10]; G3 Guardrails — quarantine (game_timed excluded from replay), timeout ≠ wrong, ESL fall-time floor, static-target selection, honest collection mapping to REAL mastery [N6, N7, N8, N9, N12]; G4 Learning-primacy — non-persistence, one-way arrow, session-only decay (multi-day rejected), never punishes a spacing-correct rest day, bkt_evidence path re-verified [N2, N4, N6]. Fail ANY gate → NO-GO until fixed. Ship LAST, behind graphux. Vendor/appeal never substitutes for a gate.

included: the four-gate CONDITIONAL-GO verdict (G1 fidelity, G2 motivation-safety, G3 guardrails, G4 learning-primacy)
the fail-any-gate = NO-GO rule and the ship-LAST-behind-graphux ordering
the vendor/appeal-never-substitutes-for-a-gate rule
excluded: the individual node mechanics it composes
implementation and styling detail (routed to graphux / other specialists)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any gate condition changes, a new drill mechanic is proposed, or a held-open decision is resolved

pros.claim: Intersecting all four gates makes the drill a defensible conditional GO instead of a vibes-based ship decision
pros.example: refusing to ship until the quarantine, timeout-not-wrong, deterministic-rise and blue-encoding gates all hold at once

cons.claim: A four-gate conjunction is deliberately hard to clear, so the drill is intentionally the last, most-fenced feature
cons.example: the drill waiting behind graphux and every gate while simpler engagement work ships first

failure_modes: issuing a GO while any one of the four gates is unmet
letting a vendor number or an appeal substitute for clearing a gate
acceptance_tests: the verdict is a conditional GO only when G1 fidelity, G2 motivation-safety, G3 guardrails and G4 learning-primacy all hold, a fail on any gate is a NO-GO until fixed, and the drill ships last behind graphux
revisit_triggers: a new drill mechanic is proposed

conflict_axes.name: speed_reward_vs_retention_invariant
conflict_axes.description: Rewarding correctness-within-a-window rewards speed, which collides with the invariant that raw speed/volume must never be rewarded over retention (INV-5).
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: fence the speed reward to automaticity-only content, quarantine its evidence, and always UI-flag it as speed not mastery

conflict_axes.name: ephemeral_meter_vs_learning_model_integrity
conflict_axes.description: A satisfying persisted meter tempts writing to the learning model, which the non-persistence and quarantine invariants forbid.
poles: persist the meter for richer feedback
keep the meter ephemeral and quarantined
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the WaterMeter non-persisted and the arrow one-way; log timed data only as game_timed excluded from replay

conflict_axes.name: session_decay_vs_spacing_correctness
conflict_axes.description: Persisting decay across days would raise session urgency but pull the learner to review early, violating spacing.
poles: persist decay across days for retention
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: restrict decay to the session and reject multi-day decay as an INV-2/INV-4 spacing violation

conflict_axes.name: variable_reward_vs_motivation_safety
conflict_axes.description: A variable-ratio schedule is more habit-forming but is a dark pattern that breaks the informational-feedback rule.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reject variable/random reward outright and require deterministic rise_per_hit

conflict_axes.name: fluency_collection_vs_honest_mastery
conflict_axes.description: A collection that lights up on drill hits feels rewarding but fabricates progress; honest collection must map to real mastery.
poles: unlock concepts on real BKT mastery
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: gate every collected concept on a real BKT mastery threshold and forbid the collection from reading the WaterMeter

conflict_axes.name: timeout_signal_vs_learner_model_honesty
conflict_axes.description: A game clock running out looks like a wrong answer, but treating it as one corrupts the learner model with a fake lapse.
poles: log a timeout as an error/Again
treat a timeout as no knowledge signal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: write no evidence on a timeout, never map it to FSRS Again, and offer an untimed re-see (INV-8)

conflict_axes.name: drill_juice_vs_construct_validity
conflict_axes.description: Cinematic drop physics and a moving target add fun but can turn a knowledge item into a reading-speed or dexterity test.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep selection on static buttons, floor the fall time for ESL fairness, and make the physics fully removable while the timer information stays

priority_rationale: The drill go/no-go and the quarantine invariant come first because they compose and protect every mechanic: nothing ships unless the four gates hold and the learning model stays firewalled. The scope-fidelity anchor, the session-decay rejection, the timeout-not-wrong rule and the variable-reward rejection come next because they are the standing constraints a later engineer is most likely to breach ('improve retention' via multi-day decay, log a timeout as Again, add a variable reward). The rise rule, content eligibility and WaterMeter model then turn the fence into the concrete deterministic mechanic; the honest encoding, timed mode, honest collection and accessibility floor finally render and constrain it. Ordering puts the guardrails and the synthesis ahead of the mechanics because on this drill the hazards, not the features, are load-bearing.

dominance_rules.rationale: the system exists to teach, so no drill mechanic may write to or degrade the learning model or scheduler
dominance_rules.trigger: a drill mechanic would write BKT/Elo/FSRS/CalibrationBin or persist decay across days
dominance_rules.action: reject or rework the mechanic so the arrow stays one-way and evidence stays quarantined

dominance_rules.rule: The four-gate verdict dominates any single appeal
dominance_rules.rationale: a conditional GO requires all of fidelity, motivation-safety, guardrails and learning-primacy at once
dominance_rules.trigger: a mechanic clears three gates but fails one
dominance_rules.action: rule it a no-go until the failed gate is fixed; a vendor number or appeal never substitutes for a gate

dominance_rules.rationale: a variable-ratio schedule is a dark pattern that breaks the informational-feedback rule
dominance_rules.trigger: a variable or random reward schedule is proposed for the meter
dominance_rules.action: require deterministic rise_per_hit and reject the variable schedule

dominance_rules.rule: Real mastery dominates fluency for any collection or progress claim
dominance_rules.rationale: lighting up a concept is a claim of learning, which drill speed cannot substantiate
dominance_rules.trigger: a collection or progress mark is about to be driven by drill hits or the WaterMeter
dominance_rules.action: gate it on a real BKT mastery threshold and forbid reading the meter

dominance_rules.rule: No knowledge signal dominates a game-clock timeout
dominance_rules.rationale: a game clock never stands in for the learner model's latency/honesty signal (INV-8)
dominance_rules.trigger: a timeout is about to be written as an error or an FSRS Again
dominance_rules.action: write no evidence, never map to Again, and offer an untimed re-see

dominance_rules.rationale: a gamified item that fails its ship gate is a broken item wearing an animation
dominance_rules.trigger: a moving target, a fixed cinematic fall time, or a reading-rate-testing timer is proposed
dominance_rules.action: keep selection on static buttons, floor the fall time for ESL fairness, and keep the MCQ ship-gated

dominance_rules.rule: Visual separation dominates reuse of the mastery language
dominance_rules.rationale: the meter must be visually unmistakable from real progress
dominance_rules.trigger: the meter is proposed in green, with a tick, or on a mastery surface
dominance_rules.action: keep it a blue stepped tickless session-labeled tank on the drill surface only

dominance_rules.rule: Re-verification dominates flag-and-trust on the evidence path
dominance_rules.rationale: the bkt_evidence path was silently broken once already
dominance_rules.action: re-verify the quarantine end-to-end rather than reverting-and-trusting the flag (INV-10)

anti_rework_rules.rule: Make the WaterMeter non-persisted from the first data model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a later teardown of a durable meter that leaked into the learning model or day-box

anti_rework_rules.rule: Log timed answers as a distinct game_timed evidence_class excluded by default from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a contaminated BKT/Elo replay that must be reconstructed after game data leaked in

anti_rework_rules.rule: Encode multi-day decay as REJECTED before any persistence is added
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a spacing-violating review-early pull shipped as a 'retention' improvement

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide timeout != wrong before wiring the drill into submitReview
anti_rework_rules.prevents: fake FSRS lapses that corrupt intervals and must be unwound

anti_rework_rules.rule: Gate the collection on real BKT mastery, never drill hits, at design time

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix rise_per_hit as deterministic before adding any reward polish
